title: Microinteractions
summary: Microinteractions give immediate, single-purpose feedback around one trigger, rule and response; motion is a communication tool, not decoration.

MUST.text: Animate only when motion clarifies cause, state change or spatial continuity.
Provide an equivalent non-motion cue (color, text, icon) for every animated state change.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion by removing or replacing non-essential motion.

SHOULD.text: Keep routine feedback animations to 100–200 ms; reserve 200–300 ms for spatial transitions.
Avoid delaying task completion; animation must not block input or navigation.

AVOID.text: Do not animate every hover, loading event or number by default.
Do not use motion as the only signal of success, error or state change.

EXAMPLE.good: "Bookmark icon fills and 'Saved' appears in 120 ms; with reduced motion, only 'Saved' appears."
EXAMPLE.bad: "Heart pulses for 1.2 s on every tap and blocks repeated taps."

FAILURE_MODES: Decorative motion competes with task content and slows completion.
Missing reduced-motion handling excludes vestibular-sensitive users.
Motion-only feedback is invisible to screen-reader and reduced-motion users.

sources.title: NN/g The Role of Animation and Motion in UX
